title: Selective receive ... after: The Mailbox Save Queue, Timeouts & after 0 Non-Blocking Flush
solutionExplanation: Uses receive ... after 0 to selectively prioritize {urgent, Payload} over {normal, Payload}, implements timeout guards, and flushes mailboxes using after 0 loops.

otpDocCards.description: Sends a message asynchronously to Dest, returning Msg. Equivalent to the ! operator.

mentalModelCheck.question: What happens to messages in an actor’s mailbox that fail to match any pattern in the currently executing `receive` block?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% Mailbox contains: [{normal, 1}, {urgent, 99}]
receive
    {urgent, Val} -> Val
end.

options.label: They are temporarily moved into the internal Save Queue while the mailbox is scanned, and automatically spliced back to the front of the mailbox once a match is found.
options.explanation: Correct! The BEAM preserves unmatched messages in an internal Save Queue. When a message matches, all saved messages are returned to the head of the mailbox in their original order.

options.label: They are permanently discarded and immediately reclaimed by the garbage collector.
options.explanation: Erlang never discards unmatched messages unless you explicitly write a catch-all clause (_ -> ok) to discard them.

options.label: They cause the process to crash immediately with a badmatch exception.
options.explanation: Unmatched receive messages never cause exceptions; the process simply moves them to the Save Queue and checks the next message.
